requirements.requirement: Install a file-integrity tool (AIDE) on node1
requirements.summary: AIDE 0.15.1-13.el7 was downloaded from CentOS vault and installed via yum localinstall after RHEL subscription repos were confirmed unavailable; rpm -q aide confirmed installation both before and after the later reboot.

requirements.requirement: Configure the tool to scope integrity monitoring to /etc
requirements.summary: aide.conf was backed up to aide.conf.orig and rewritten with a FULL rule (permissions/inode/owner/group/size/mtime/ctime/acl/selinux/xattrs/md5+sha256) applied specifically to '/etc', with narrow exclusions for routinely-changing files (mtab, adjtime, the backup itself).

requirements.requirement: Initialize and activate an integrity baseline database
requirements.summary: aide --init produced aide.db.new.gz, which was copied to the active aide.db.gz, and an immediate aide --check returned 'All files match AIDE database. Looks okay!' (exit 0), establishing a clean initial baseline.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate the baseline can actually identify later changes to /etc (not just be configured)
requirements.summary: A reversible functional test added /etc/aide-selftest-marker.txt and AIDE correctly reported it as 'added'; after removal, AIDE correctly flagged the resulting /etc directory mtime/ctime change, then the baseline was re-initialized to a clean state and reconfirmed clean.

requirements.requirement: Provide an ongoing mechanism to report future changes
requirements.summary: A weekly cron job (/etc/cron.d/aide-check) was created to run aide --check and log to /var/log/aide/aide.log, and the cron file was confirmed present pre-restart; the post-restart check (before a script early-exit) also showed the cron file was still in place at /etc/cron.d.

overall_summary: The core task — establishing a functional AIDE-based integrity baseline scoped to /etc on node1 — is well supported by direct evidence: the tool was installed despite no subscription repos being enabled, configuration scoped to /etc with a comprehensive rule set, an initial clean baseline was captured, and a reversible add/remove self-test proved the baseline actually detects changes (not merely that it was configured). A weekly cron job was added for ongoing reporting. The executor additionally ran the independent node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot_id (e9250ad1...) and post-restart boot_id (9655a8b7...) both match the fixed before-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots exactly, corroborating a genuine reboot; the AIDE database persisted unchanged through the reboot and correctly flagged a legitimate DHCP-driven resolv.conf change, after which the baseline was refreshed to a clean state. One gap: the post-restart verification command (cmd-d7e2cd673c8c4f57) appears to have exited early (pipefail interacting with aide --check's nonzero exit) before its cron/crond-status lines executed, so post-reboot persistence of the cron job and crond service state was not directly re-confirmed in this run, only pre-restart.
limitations: The post-restart command cmd-d7e2cd673c8c4f57 likely exited early due to set -euo pipefail catching AIDE's nonzero exit code from the --check | tail pipeline, so its planned cron-file and 'systemctl is-active crond' checks were never actually executed/captured — post-reboot persistence of the cron reporting job is inferred from pre-restart evidence, not directly re-observed post-restart.
Leftover scratch files in /tmp (rpm and several aide-check log files) were not cleaned up; low risk since /tmp is outside the monitored /etc scope, but noted for completeness.
package-health snapshots were unavailable (timed out) both before and after, so no independent package-consistency cross-check was possible.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands trace cleanly to the task: one early large command (cmd-2482a17c68d04bcd) partially failed mid-script (set -e tripped on a PATH check) but had already installed the aide package and created/removed an empty /etc/aide.conf.d directory with no residue; a subsequent attempt (cmd-6a12a94d7e4d416f) failed before any writes occurred (no state change). The successful config write, database init/activation, functional self-test (file added then removed, cleanly reverted), cron job creation, and post-test/post-reboot baseline refreshes were all clearly purposeful. The only residue is a handful of scratch artifacts left in /tmp (aide-0.15.1-13.el7.x86_64.rpm, several aide-check-*.log files, reboot.log), visible in the after_executor snapshot but not present in /etc; this is low-risk and outside the monitored scope, so it is a minor deduction rather than a significant hygiene issue. No unsafe exposure, broad/destructive mutation, or damaged package state was observed.
